simon: Heads-up: ran a 6h overnight perf sweep on mixed serving traffic (chat+embed) across A10/T4/L4/A100/H100. Found a tail-latency regression on H100 when max_tokens_per_batch >= 120000. Putting raw logs + a short summary here.

mariam: ugh. can you paste the profiler output?

simon: paste: ```
H100 run @ max_tokens_batch=150000
- p50 latency: 22ms
- p95 latency: 310ms (↑ 2.6x vs baseline)
- p99 latency: 640ms (↑ 3.1x)
- GPU util: 72%
- kernel switch count: 3.9M (vs A100 1.1M)
- avg KV cache fragmentation: 18%
```

ryan: interesting — kernel switch count jumps. I bet we're hitting a kernel-selection path that prefers fallback kernels for very long batches on H100. Those fallbacks have worse parallelism and blow up stall cycles.

ashley: also the KV fragmentation number stands out. If requests pack many discontiguous prefixes, we end up with more KV page merges and more memcpy. H100 memory bandwidth cost + fallback kernels = p99 disaster.

perf-bot: auto-note: regression window detected between 1718800000 and 1718883333. Added perf-alert ticket PERF-873.

mariam: From the sweep I saw a similar but milder effect on A100 at >140k tokens, but T4/L4 and A10 are fine up to their usual caps. We should avoid a one-size cap.

simon: proposal: per-device policy with three knobs -> max_concurrent_batch_tokens, max_batch_size, kv_pack_threshold. Initial suggestion: H100: 110k tokens, A100: 130k, L4: 80k, A10: 95k, T4: 70k. kv_pack_threshold default 0.6 (pack only when prefix reuse >= 60%).

ryan: +1 but we need to be explicit about kernel-selector hints. When estimated effective_sequence_length > 4k, prefer kernel-family B (vectorized tiled) otherwise family A. Also add a hard ceiling preventing fallback chain if kernel_switch_count per-second > 500k.

ashley: can we add a cheap prefilter in the queue that computes an "estimated KV fragmentation" score per request (based on prefix hashes) and gate packing? cheap bitset probe should be O(1) per req.

mariam: agree. My microbenchmark suggests the probe cost is ~0.4ms per request but saves ~6-20% kernel time on H100 for bad packs. Worth it.

simon: action items:
- ryan: add kernel-selector hint and switch-rate guard (PR + unit tests)
- ashley: prototype KV-fragment probe in queueing layer, run canary on H100 ring
- mariam: run a constrained rerun with the proposed token caps and collect p50/p95/p99 + kernel-switch traces
- perf-bot: attach PERF-873 to the PRs and gate CI perf baseline.

ryan: I'll target the PR today, adding a flag `--enable-switch-guard` so we can toggle. snippet: ```json
{"device_policies": {"H100": {"max_tokens_batch": 110000, "max_batch_size": 48, "kernel_hint": "B", "switch_guard": true}}}```

ashley: I'll ship a prototype branch `kv-prefilter/h100-canary` and run 30m steady-state. @perf-bot can you reserve two H100 nodes for the canary between 0900-1100 UTC? :pray:

perf-bot: reserved nodes: h100-canary-01,h100-canary-02 (0900-1100 UTC). Ticket PERF-873 updated.

mariam: one more thought — make the caps percentile-driven. e.g., set H100 cap to 95th percentile of historical per-batch token distribution for high-variance tenants, and relax for low-variance. That prevents overconstraining small tenants.

simon: good plan. let's run canary then iterate. If the H100 p99 drops back near baseline we adopt the per-device defaults and add telemetry to auto-tune per-working-set.

ryan: noted. I'll include telemetry hooks (kernel_switch_rate, kv_frag_score, per_batch_tokens) so Optimize can build a suggestion job later.

ashley: thanks folks. will post canary logs once finished. :thumbsup:

simon: thanks — filing short RFC after canary.
